status: Rust source now uses support-aware Hermitian PSD square root; exact-head Rust runner validation pending independent NumPy reference
claim_ceiling: The result concerns one-qubit message/reference, one-qubit black-hole/early-radiation, and a single Haar U(4) scrambler. It establishes Petz optimality for this specific maximally-mixed finite-dimensional channel family when the commutator criterion is numerically satisfied. It is not a large-N decoder result, a gate-efficient implementation, gravitational evaporation, or a QES/island calculation.

reference.paper: Bikun Li, Zhaoyou Wang, Guo Zheng, Yat Wong, Liang Jiang, Optimality Condition for the Petz Map
reference.theorem: For logical input rho and Petz reference sigma, when [rho,sigma]=0, Petz recovery is entanglement-fidelity optimal iff [M_sigma, gamma tensor T]=0, with gamma=sigma^(-1/2)rho and T=Tr_L[(gamma^dagger tensor I_K)sqrt(M_sigma)].
reference.general_theorem: The paper's general necessary-and-sufficient condition is B=sqrt(M_sigma)(gamma tensor T) >= 0. The commutator test is the commuting-rho/sigma specialization used here.

channel.scrambler: Haar U(4) acting on M tensor B
channel.channel: N:M -> A=E tensor R, with Bprime as the inaccessible channel environment

qec_matrix.partial_trace_checks: Tr_K M_sigma=I_L/2 by channel trace preservation; Tr_L M_sigma=I_K/2 for this unitary/Bell-pair channel construction.

optimality_test.interpretation: For rho=sigma=I/2, a numerically vanishing commutator is the theorem's necessary-and-sufficient criterion for Petz entanglement-fidelity optimality in this channel.
optimality_test.inverse_square_root: Removed from the QI-4O QEC-matrix square-root route; the QI-4P Petz recovery channel still separately needs an inverse square root of rho_A and retains its own unregularized Newton-Schulz policy.

optimality_matrix_square_root.method: 8x8 real-symmetric embedding eigendecomposition with real eigenvectors mapped to complex 4-vectors and complex Gram-Schmidt
optimality_matrix_square_root.support: Positive-semidefinite matrices including rank-deficient cases; numerical support rank reported
optimality_matrix_square_root.negative_spectrum: Materially negative eigenvalues are rejected; only negative roundoff within the declared tolerance is treated as zero
optimality_matrix_square_root.flooring: No positive eigenvalue floor or support regularization is applied
authored_controls: rank-one PSD projector square root equals itself
rank-two PSD diagonal matrix reconstructs to declared tolerance
materially negative eigenvalue returns a typed non-positive error

independent_numpy_comparator.generator: Independent NumPy PRNG; complex Gaussian Haar U(4) via QR; direct Kraus/QEC-matrix construction; numpy.linalg.eigh for sqrt(M_sigma); explicit partial trace and commutator.
independent_numpy_comparator.caveat: Independent NumPy PRNG and eigendecomposition; not bitwise ChaCha20 Rust output or a Rust execution receipt.

limitations: The theorem applies to a fixed channel and stated input/reference states; this test does not generalize to non-maximally-mixed inputs.
A vanishing commutator says the Petz map is optimal for entanglement fidelity in this finite channel; it does not measure gate count or hardware cost.
No exact SDP is needed when the theorem criterion is satisfied, but an independent SDP or certified bound remains required for future cases where the criterion fails.
The 2-dimensional logical/environment setting is too small to infer large-N Hayden-Preskill scaling.
